sentences.text: The meeting was held with Gareth Pryce (client) and Helen Moss (solicitor) to discuss the estate of his deceased mother.
The client's mother died in June and left the house on Wyvern Road to the client and his brother Neil, fifty-fifty.
The client and Neil are both named as executors of the will.
Probate has not yet been applied for.
Neil refuses to sign probate documents and states he is not moving out of the house.
An estate agent valued the house at approximately £280,000, though Neil prevented a proper valuation by not allowing entry.
The client describes the relationship with Neil as 'bad' and 'really bad'.
On Saturday, 7 November, the client went to the house to collect Mum's paperwork and argued with Neil in the kitchen about the sale.
Neil punched the client in the face without warning.
Neil broke the client's nose, causing blood everywhere.
The client was treated at Castlebrook General A&E, where an X-ray confirmed a broken nose.
After being punched, Neil picked up a kitchen chair and hit the client across the back and shoulder, causing bruising that lasted for a week.
The client states Neil did not have a knife, though he expressed fear that Neil might have used one if he had had access.
The client drove himself to the hospital after the incident.
The client has not yet reported the assault to the police, citing his mother's likely objection.
The client possesses a hospital discharge letter, photos of his face taken the next day, and the will.
Neil has sent texts stating the client deserved the assault and is not receiving any money.
The client requests the house to be sold and the mother's estate to be sorted.
The client requests Neil to stay away from him.
The solicitor advised that as joint executors, both parties must act, but the court can be applied to remove Neil if he refuses to co-operate.
The solicitor advised writing a letter to Neil setting a deadline.
The solicitor strongly advised the client to report the assault to the police.
The solicitor advised the client could apply to family court for a non-molestation order to stop Neil from contacting him or coming near him.
The solicitor stated executor work is usually paid for from the estate.
The solicitor will send a client care letter detailing fees by Friday.
The client is to send screenshots of texts, the discharge letter, photos, and the will to the solicitor by Monday, 30th.
The solicitor will draft a letter to Neil regarding the estate and send it to the client for approval by Wednesday, 2nd of December.
The solicitor offered to assist the client if he decides to go to the police.
The solicitor booked the client for an appointment on the 9th of December.
